target.statement: IG-Diff (illumination-guided diffusion) achieves 26.03 dB PSNR and 0.922 SSIM on the LOL-Raindrop complex night-scene test set, the best among all compared enhancement/restoration baselines.
target.table_ref: Table 2 (Quantitative comparison on low-light adverse weather dataset), row LOL-Raindrop, column 'Ours'
target.dataset: LOL-Raindrop (synthesized from the public Raindrop dataset [24] via the paper's EC-Zero-DCE + weather-degradation pipeline; 861 train / 58 test pairs)

compute.basis: No code/configs are released, so the agent must re-cloning the entire data-synthesis pipeline (EC-Zero-DCE reversed Zero-DCE darkening + weather compositing) and train the illumination-guided diffusion U-Net (1000 diffusion steps, 40 sampling steps, 64x64 patches, cross-attention illumination injection) from scratch, which the authors ran on a single RTX 4090Ti and which translates to ~100 hours of CPU-only command time plus patch-wise sampling on the 58 test images.

blockers: No code, weights or configs released (PDF link list is empty)

Data is not provided; the complex night-scene dataset must be regenerated by reimplementing the EC-Zero-DCE darkening curve and weather compositing (raindrops/rain/snow/fog/haze) on top of the public source datasets
Requires the pretrained SCI illumination estimator [21] and the pretrained EC-Zero-DCE/LEDNet models as external dependencies

Target number requires training a conditional diffusion model from scratch on a GPU (authors used a single RTX 4090Ti); no training schedule, iteration count or batch size is given, only lr 2e-5 and EMA 0.999
Patch-based inference over 40 sampling steps per patch is additionally expensive at test time
title: IG-Diff: Complex Night Scene Restoration with Illumination-Guided Diffusion Model
